q: Which part of a plant fixes it firmly into the soil and absorbs water?
e: Roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb water and minerals.

q: A pumpkin plant grows along the ground and bears heavy fruit. It is classified as a:
e: Creepers have weak stems and spread horizontally along the ground.

q: A Grade 1 student believes a bat is a bird because it flies. Which fact best corrects this misconception?
a: Bats give birth to babies and feed them milk.
w: Bats eat insects instead of grains.
Bats fly only during the nighttime.
e: Bats are mammals because they give birth to live young and nurse them.

q: Which of the following domestic animals is kept in a shed built by humans?
e: Cows are housed in sheds, while horses live in stables and dogs in kennels.

q: Which group of food items mainly helps young children grow bigger and stronger?
e: Protein-rich foods like milk, eggs, and pulses are body-building foods.

q: Children often misidentify plant parts used as food. Which item is a root of a plant?
e: Carrots are taproots, whereas potatoes and onions are modified stems.

q: What is the main natural source of fresh water on Earth that fills ponds and rivers?
e: Rain is the primary natural source that replenishes surface water bodies.

q: Which simple method makes tap water safe for drinking by killing harmful germs?
e: Boiling water kills disease-causing germs, making it safe to drink.

q: A family consisting of parents, children, grandparents, uncles, and cousins living together is a:
e: A joint family includes multiple generations living under one roof.

q: Where should a person go in the neighborhood to buy postage stamps and send letters?
e: Post offices handle mail services and sell postal items like stamps.

q: Which type of shelter is temporary, portable, and made of strong canvas cloth?
e: Tents are temporary movable shelters made of heavy cloth.

q: Why are cotton clothes preferred during the summer season in India?
a: They absorb sweat and keep us cool.
w: They trap body heat to warm us.
e: Cotton permits air flow and absorbs body sweat, keeping the wearer cool.

q: Air cannot be seen, but its presence can be felt. Which observation shows moving air?
w: A stone sinking in a bucket
e: Wind exerts a force that moves lightweight objects like leaves.

q: Which sense organ helps a child distinguish between a soft whistle sound and a loud bell?
e: Ears receive sound vibrations and enable the sense of hearing.

q: While teaching traffic safety to Grade 1, what does the yellow signal light mean?
e: Yellow light warns drivers to slow down and prepare to stop or go.

q: In which season do many trees shed their leaves while the weather cools down?
e: Trees shed leaves during autumn in preparation for winter.

q: To prevent germ transmission, when is washing hands with soap most essential?
a: Before meals and after using the toilet
w: Only after waking up in the morning
Only when hands look visibly dirty
e: Handwashing before eating and after toilet use stops disease transmission.

q: Students often think all green plant parts prepare food. Which part is mainly called the food factory?
e: Leaves contain chlorophyll and conduct photosynthesis to make plant food.

q: What bright celestial object seen during daytime gives Earth heat and light, and is actually a star?
e: The Sun is a star at the center of our solar system.

q: Which community helper comes to our home to repair broken water pipes and leaking taps?
e: Plumbers install and repair water pipes, taps, and drainage systems.

q: Rose and hibiscus plants have hard, woody stems but do not grow as tall as banyan trees. Under which category are they classified in standard primary EVS?
e: Shrubs are medium-sized plants with hard, woody stems branching near the ground.

q: Grade 1 children often confuse whales with fish because both live in water. What basic characteristic proves a whale is a mammal?
a: It gives birth to live babies and feeds them milk.
w: It swims using powerful tail movements.
It lives exclusively in deep ocean waters.
It has a streamlined body shape.
e: Whales are mammals because they give birth to live young and nurse them, unlike fish which lay eggs.

q: Fruits like oranges and apples help protect our body from illnesses. Which category of food do they belong to in primary EVS?
e: Fruits and vegetables are rich in vitamins and minerals, helping us fight diseases as protective foods.

q: When water vapor in the air touches a cold glass surface, tiny water drops appear. What is this process called?
e: Condensation occurs when invisible water vapor cools down and turns back into liquid water drops.

q: Which internal body organ works continuously like a pump to send blood throughout our body?
e: The heart pumps blood continuously to transport nutrients and oxygen across the body.

q: A family consisting of only a mother, a father, and their one or two children is known as a:
e: A nuclear family includes parents and their children living together in one home.

q: Which community helper protects our city or village from fire hazards and rescues people from burning buildings?
e: Firefighters respond to fire emergencies and rescue people trapped in burning structures.

q: Houses built on sturdy wooden pillars above ground level in heavy rainfall areas like Assam are called:
e: Stilt houses are elevated on poles to protect homes from flooding and damp soil.

q: Why do people wear woollen clothes during the winter season in northern India?
a: Wool traps body heat and keeps us warm.
w: Wool allows cool air to reach our skin.
Wool keeps rain water away from the body.
e: Woollen fibres trap air, which acts as an insulator preventing body heat from escaping.

q: While crossing a busy road on foot, pedestrians should always use which marked pathway?
e: Zebra crossings are black and white stripes on roads marked specifically for pedestrian safety.

q: When a student blows air into an empty rubber balloon, it expands and becomes heavier. This simple experiment shows that air:
w: Is made only of water vapor
Always moves in an upward direction
e: Air occupies space inside the balloon causing expansion and adds measurable mass to it.

q: Why does the Moon appear to change its shape night after night when viewed from Earth?
a: We see different illuminated portions of the Moon as it moves around Earth.
w: The Moon physically grows bigger and smaller each day.
Clouds cover different parts of the Moon every night.
The Sun casts a shadowy veil over the Moon daily.
e: Moon phases occur because we see varying amounts of the sunlit side of the Moon as it orbits Earth.

q: Animals like cows, deer, and goats eat only plants and plant products. What are they called?
e: Animals that consume only plant matter are classified as herbivores.

q: Which Indian season comes right after winter, when the weather becomes pleasant and many colorful flowers bloom?
e: Spring is the mild post-winter season associated with fresh leaves and flowering plants.

q: Why should nail clippers be used regularly to trim fingernails short in young children?
a: Dirt and harmful germs accumulate easily under long nails.
w: Long nails prevent fingers from growing properly.
Short nails help children write faster in class.
Trimming nails makes the skin turn softer.
e: Short fingernails prevent mud and harmful micro-organisms from collecting underneath.

q: A Grade 1 child thinks seeds need dark soil to grow because seeds only sprout underground. What is actually required inside a seed to begin sprouting?
e: Germination requires water, oxygen, and suitable warmth; soil is not strictly required for the sprouting process itself.

q: Which animal makes its own home by weaving twigs and grass together in trees?
e: Birds build nests using twigs, grass, and leaves to lay eggs and shelter their young.

q: Which action directly helps conserve water at home during daily routines?
a: Turning off the tap while brushing teeth
w: Washing cars daily using an open hosepipe
Boiling double the amount of drinking water
e: Closing running taps while brushing prevents unnecessary wastage of fresh water.

q: Green and blue dustbins are placed in public places. What should ideally be thrown into the green bin?
a: Wet kitchen waste like vegetable peels
w: Dry plastic wrappers and broken bottles
e: Green dustbins are used for biodegradable wet waste like food scraps and plant leaves.

q: Pea plants and money plants have weak stems that need support like a stick or wall to grow upwards. They are known as:
e: Climbers have weak stems and produce special structures to climb up external supports.

q: Small plants with soft, green, non-woody stems such as mint and coriander belong to which plant category?
e: Small plants with delicate green stems are classified as herbs.

q: A Grade 1 student claims a potato is a root because it grows underground. How can a teacher correct this misconception?
a: Explain that potatoes have eyes or buds, which are features of stems.
w: Explain that roots are always red or white in color.
Explain that underground parts are always classified as roots.
Explain that potatoes contain seeds inside them.
e: Potatoes possess nodes and buds known as eyes, which are characteristic of underground stems.

q: Animals like bears and crows eat both plant parts and the flesh of other animals. What are they called?
e: Organisms that feed on both plant material and meat are classified as omnivores.

q: Grade 1 children often confuse spiders with insects. How do insects fundamentally differ from spiders in body structure?
a: Insects have six legs, whereas spiders have eight legs.
w: Insects live only in water, whereas spiders live on land.
Insects do not lay eggs, whereas spiders lay eggs.
Insects have bones, whereas spiders do not.
e: Insects are hexapods with six legs, while arachnids like spiders have eight legs.

q: Which group of food items primarily provides energy to our body for daily activities like playing and running?
e: Carbohydrates serve as the primary source of energy for daily physical activities.

q: Which of the following food items is usually eaten raw as part of a fresh salad?
e: Cucumbers are edible uncooked and commonly consumed fresh in salads.

q: When ice cubes kept in a bowl gradually change into liquid water at room temperature, which process takes place?
e: Melting is the process where a solid turns into a liquid when exposed to heat or room temperature.

q: Why is ocean or sea water unsuitable for drinking directly by human beings?
a: It contains a high amount of dissolved salts.
w: It lacks oxygen for humans to breathe.
It has a lower temperature than river water.
It does not contain any living organisms.
e: Saline water from oceans contains excessive dissolved salts that cause dehydration.

q: In standard family relationship terminology, what is a person's father's mother called?
e: Relatives on the father's side use the prefix paternal, so a father's mother is the paternal grandmother.

q: What type of special house floats on water bodies and is commonly found in Kashmir and Kerala?
e: Houseboats are floating shelters constructed on wooden boats for living on lakes and backwaters.

q: Why do houses in hilly areas with heavy snowfall or rainfall have sloping roofs?
a: To let rain and snow slide down easily.
w: To keep birds from nesting on top.
To absorb maximum sunlight during daytime.
To allow occupants to walk safely on the roof.
e: Sloping roofs prevent waterlogging and accumulation of snow on house tops.

q: Which community helper is primarily responsible for maintaining law, order, and safety in our society?
e: Police officers enforce laws and protect citizens from crimes and disorder.

q: Which organ is the largest sense organ in the human body that helps us feel pain, pressure, and temperature?
e: Skin covers the entire body surface and houses receptors for touch, temperature, and pain.

q: During which season in India do people commonly use raincoats, umbrellas, and gumboots when stepping outdoors?
e: The monsoon season brings heavy rains, requiring protective gear like raincoats and umbrellas.

q: Why should children be strictly advised never to touch electrical switches with wet hands?
a: Water conducts electricity and can cause an electric shock.
w: Water damages the paint on the wall switch.
Wet hands turn off the electricity supply permanently.
Water makes the switch too slippery to press.
e: Unpurified water conducts electric current, posing a severe risk of electric shock.

q: Why is brushing teeth twice a day essential for maintaining good oral health in children?
a: It removes trapped food particles and prevents tooth decay.
w: It permanently changes teeth color from white to yellow.
It replaces missing milk teeth instantly.
e: Brushing removes food residues and plaque that lead to dental cavities.

q: What causes the regular cycle of day and night on Earth every 24 hours?
a: The rotation of the Earth on its axis.
w: The revolution of the Earth around the Sun.
The movement of the Sun around the Earth.
The rotation of the Moon on its axis.
e: Earth's rotation on its axis exposes different sides to the Sun, producing day and night.

q: Which part of a flowering plant usually attracts insects with its color and later develops into a fruit?
e: Flowers are reproductive structures of plants that develop into seed-bearing fruits after pollination.

q: What is the young one of a sheep called?
e: A baby sheep is called a lamb, whereas a baby goat is a kid and a baby cow is a calf.

q: Why is planting more trees recommended for protecting our environment?
a: Trees release oxygen and keep the air clean.
w: Trees reduce the total rainfall in an area.
Trees stop plants from growing near them.
Trees absorb all sunlight and make Earth dark.
e: Trees produce oxygen during photosynthesis and absorb air pollutants, improving environmental quality.

q: A primary teacher shows children a pumpkin plant creeping on the ground. Which structural feature prevents it from growing upright like a tree?
a: Thick heavy fruit and weak stem
e: Pumpkin plants are creepers with soft, weak stems that cannot support heavy fruits upright.

q: Which of the following plants is categorized as a herb based on stem characteristics taught in Grade 2 EVS?
e: Coriander has a soft and green stem, which is characteristic of herbs.

q: When explaining animal shelters, why does a rabbit dig a burrow underground?
a: To stay safe from predators and heat
w: Because it cannot breathe on land
e: Rabbits dig burrows primarily for protection against predators and harsh weather conditions.

q: Which of these animals is correctly classified as a carnivore in primary school EVS lessons?
e: Leopards eat only the flesh of other animals, making them carnivores.

q: While teaching animal offspring names, which pair should the teacher identify as INCORRECT?
e: A baby duck is called a duckling, whereas a joey is the baby of a kangaroo.

q: A child brings boiled eggs and pulses in their lunchbox. Under which primary food group do these items fall?
e: Eggs and pulses are rich in proteins, which help the body grow and repair tissues.

q: Which of the following items is usually eaten raw after washing, without cooking?
e: Cucumber is a salad vegetable eaten raw, whereas rice, potato, and kidney beans require cooking.

q: What is the main natural source of fresh water on Earth introduced in Grade 2 EVS?
e: Rain is the primary natural source of fresh water that replenishes water bodies on Earth.

q: A teacher pours water into a glass, a bowl, and a bottle. What property of water does this activity demonstrate?
e: Water takes the shape of the container it is poured into because it has no definite shape.

q: A teacher balances two inflated balloons on a stick and punctures one balloon. What property of air does this activity prove?
e: The stick tilts toward the inflated balloon, showing that air inside it adds weight.

q: Why are houses with sloping roofs commonly constructed in regions with heavy rain or snow?
a: To let water and snow slide off easily
w: To make the house look taller
To trap extra heat inside the roof
To store extra grains on top
e: Sloped roofs allow rainwater and snow to drain quickly without damaging the house.

q: Which shelter type is portable and commonly used by campers or nomads?
e: Tents are made of canvas or lightweight material and can be easily moved from place to place.

q: A family consisting of parents, children, grandparents, uncles, aunts, and cousins living together is called a:
e: A joint family consists of several generations of relatives sharing a single home.

q: How should a teacher clarify the distinct role of a cobbler compared to a tailor?
a: Cobblers repair shoes while tailors stitch clothes
w: Cobblers build houses while tailors mend shoes
Cobblers grow crops while tailors sell medicine
Cobblers extinguish fires while tailors drive buses
e: Cobblers work with footwear, whereas tailors sew and mend garments.

q: Which natural fiber comes from an animal source and is used to make warm clothing?
e: Wool is obtained from the fur of sheep or goats, making it an animal-based natural fiber.

q: Which mode of transport is the fastest for traveling across continents?
e: Aeroplanes travel through the air at high speeds, making air transport the fastest mode.

q: What does a yellow traffic signal light indicate to drivers on the road?
e: The yellow traffic light alerts drivers to slow down and prepare to stop or proceed carefully.

q: What causes day and night on Earth as taught in early primary science lessons?
a: Rotation of the Earth on its axis
w: Movement of the Sun around Earth
Moon coming between Earth and Sun
e: As the Earth rotates on its axis, the part facing the Sun experiences day while the opposite side experiences night.

q: Which student action demonstrates correct waste segregation habits at school?
a: Putting banana peels in a green waste bin
w: Burning dry leaves in the playground
Dumping plastic bags in garden soil
Flushing paper towels down the toilet
e: Organic wet waste like fruit peels should be placed in green bins for composting.

q: Low-lying flat land situated between two mountains or hills is called a:
e: A valley is a low area of land between hills or mountains, often containing a stream or river.

q: A student notices that a money plant coils around a wooden stick to grow upward. How should the teacher classify this plant based on stem strength?
e: Climbers have weak stems and take support of external structures to grow vertically.

q: To correct the misconception that all edible plant parts growing underground are roots, which example should a teacher use for an underground stem?
e: Potato is a modified underground stem (tuber), whereas carrot, radish, and turnip are roots.

q: Which animal home is artificially constructed by humans to keep domestic horses safe?
e: Horses are kept in man-made shelters called stables.

q: When teaching about animal movement, how should a teacher describe animals like frogs that live both on land and in water?
e: Animals capable of living both in water and on land are classified as amphibians.

q: Which group of food items is classified under body-building foods in early primary science?
e: Proteins like milk, pulses, and fish build body tissues and promote growth.

q: What term is used for the light meal usually taken in the late afternoon or early evening?
e: A light bite eaten between lunch and dinner is referred to as a snack.

q: Which action taught in Grade 2 EVS represents rainwater harvesting at a basic level?
a: Collecting rainwater in buckets to water garden plants
w: Using hosepipes to clean house verandas
e: Collecting and utilizing rainwater directly for household tasks is basic rainwater harvesting.

q: When boiling water turns into steam, which state of matter does water change into?
e: Steam is water in its gaseous state.

q: What is gentle and pleasant moving air called in primary weather lessons?
e: Soft and light moving air is called a breeze.

q: Which national emergency telephone helpline number in India is used to call the police station?
e: 100 is the standard emergency contact number for police assistance in India.

q: Which community helper installs and repairs electrical wires, switches, and appliances in houses?
e: Electricians specialize in fixing electrical circuits and appliances.

q: Which material combination is typically used to build durable pucca houses in cities?
e: Pucca houses are permanent structures made of sturdy materials like bricks, cement, and iron.

q: Why do people wear dark-colored woolen clothes during the winter season?
a: They keep the body warm by trapping heat
w: They absorb sweat quickly from the body
They allow cool air to pass through easily
They reflect all sunlight away from the skin
e: Woolen fabrics trap air pockets that prevent body heat from escaping.

q: Which mode of communication is used to send written messages or printed documents instantly across the world via internet?
e: Email delivers digital text messages instantly using internet networks.

q: What is the safest place for pedestrians to walk alongside a busy road?
e: Footpaths are designated raised walkways alongside roads specifically for pedestrians.

q: If a child faces the rising Sun in the morning, which cardinal direction lies to their left arm side?
e: Facing East places North to the left side and South to the right side.

q: Why does the Sun appear much larger and brighter than other stars visible in the night sky?
a: It is much closer to Earth than other stars
w: It is the only star that produces its own heat
It burns liquid fuel instead of hot gases
It stays inside the Earth's atmosphere
e: The Sun is the closest star to Earth, making it look larger and brighter than distant stars.

q: Why should children be taught to cover their mouth and nose while sneezing?
a: To prevent germs from spreading through air to others
w: To prevent cold air from entering their lungs
To keep their hands warm during winter
To stop dust particles from entering their eyes
e: Covering the nose and mouth stops respiratory droplets containing germs from polluting ambient air.

q: Which sense organ informs us about the fragrance of a rose or the smell of burning paper?
e: The olfactory receptors in the nose detect various scents and odors.

q: Which gas present in the air do green plants absorb during daytime to prepare their food?
e: Plants take in carbon dioxide from air to carry out photosynthesis during the day.

q: Which structural characteristic distinguishes a shrub from a herb in early plant classification?
a: It has a hard, woody stem branching near the ground.
w: It has a soft, green, and non-woody stem.
It grows thick trunks reaching great heights.
It requires support to stand upright.
e: Shrubs have medium height with thin, hard, woody stems that branch out close to the base.

q: A teacher asks students to identify an omnivore commonly found around human settlements. Which animal should be highlighted?
e: Crows eat both plant material and meat, making them omnivores.

q: Which bird builds its nest by stitching leaves together using plant threads or spider silk?
e: Tailorbirds use their sharp beaks like needles to stitch leaves together for shelter.

q: Which pair of food items is primarily classified as energy-giving food in primary science lessons?
e: Rice and potatoes are rich in carbohydrates, providing quick energy to the body.

q: Water droplets appear on the outer surface of a glass filled with ice-cold water. What process causes this?
w: Evaporation of water from inside the glass
Leakage of water through tiny pores in glass
Freezing of liquid water on the outer wall
e: Water vapor present in the surrounding air cools down and condenses upon contacting the cold glass surface.

q: What is fast and strong moving air that causes damage to trees and roofs called?
e: Very high-speed, strong wind accompanied by rain or thunder is termed a storm.

q: Which internal organ works non-stop to pump blood across the entire human body?
e: The heart acts as a muscular pump to circulate blood throughout the body continuously.

q: In regions prone to frequent heavy rain and floods, on what structures are houses constructed to stay safe?
e: Stilt houses are raised above the ground on strong wooden or bamboo poles to keep floodwater out.

q: A family consisting of only parents and their one or two children living together is classified as a:
e: A small family comprising only parents and children is known as a nuclear family.

q: Which community helper is specifically trained to sell medicines prescribed by doctors?
e: A chemist or pharmacist dispenses and sells medicines to patients.

q: Which mode of water transport is built to operate under the surface of the sea?
e: Submarines are specialized vessels capable of traveling completely underwater.

q: What is the immediate help given to an injured person at the scene of an accident called?
e: First aid is the initial, temporary medical assistance provided before professional healthcare arrives.

q: Why does the illuminated shape of the Moon change continuously when viewed from Earth throughout the month?
a: We see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits Earth.
w: The Moon physically expands and shrinks every few days.
Earth casts a total dark shadow on the Moon every night.
Clouds cover different fractions of the Moon daily.
e: The changing positions of the Moon relative to the Sun and Earth reveal varying portions of its illuminated surface.

q: Why are light-colored cotton clothes preferred during hot summer days?
a: They absorb sweat and reflect heat to keep the body cool.
w: They trap body heat to prevent sweating.
They absorb maximum sunlight to brighten clothes.
They are waterproof and block cool winds.
e: Cotton permits air circulation and absorbs sweat, while light colors reflect solar heat.

q: Which medium provides news, educational content, and entertainment to millions of people at the exact same time?
e: Television is a mass communication medium capable of broadcasting messages to large audiences simultaneously.

q: A raised area of land with a steep side and a flat elevated top is known as a:
e: A plateau is elevated land with a flat summit, often referred to as a tableland.

q: What is the young, crawling larval stage of a butterfly called?
e: The larva that hatches from a butterfly egg is called a caterpillar.

q: Why are children instructed to clean their teeth before going to sleep at night?
a: To remove trapped food particles that attract decay-causing bacteria.
w: To change the color of teeth from white to yellow.
To produce excess saliva for night digestion.
To prevent saliva from forming during sleep.
e: Nightly brushing removes leftover food bits so mouth bacteria cannot grow and damage teeth overnight.

q: Which plant structure contains the tiny baby plant inside and grows into a seedling?
e: A seed holds the embryo of a plant along with food storage needed for germination.

q: Which local facility is primarily used by citizens to open savings accounts and deposit money securely?
e: Banks provide safe storage for money and offer personal financial services.

q: Which bird uses its sharp beak like a needle to stitch leaves together with thread or fiber to build its nest?
e: The tailorbird stitches leaves together using plant fibers to craft its nest.

q: Which of the following trees leaves are long, thin, with serrated edges, and widely known in India for medicinal properties?
e: Neem leaves have serrated margins and are traditionally used for their antibacterial properties.

q: What is the primary source of natural freshwater that replenishes surface bodies like ponds, rivers, and lakes in India?
e: Rainfall is the main natural source that fills ponds, rivers, and lakes.

q: Why does the Grade 3 EVS syllabus refer to a child's family as their first school?
a: Children learn basic values and social behavior first from family members
w: Parents teach children how to read and write formal textbooks at home
Children spend all twenty-four hours of their day only inside their home
Family members act as certified classroom teachers before primary school
e: Primary socialization and foundational learning begin within the family circle.

q: In the chapter 'Chhotu's House', what key conceptual understanding about a shelter is highlighted?
a: A structure becomes a home when divided into functional areas for daily life
w: Only permanent brick houses can protect human beings from hot sun and heavy rain
Open drainage pipes are safer places to live than concrete buildings
Houses must always be built using expensive commercial materials
e: The story emphasizes that living spaces are defined by how human beings organize their daily activities.

q: Tapioca (Kappa) is a underground root food commonly boiled and eaten with fish curry in which Indian state?
e: Boiled tapioca served with spicy fish curry is a traditional staple dish of Kerala.

q: In Indian classical dance forms, hand gestures and facial expressions used to convey feelings without speaking are known as:
e: Mudras (hand gestures) and Bhavas (facial expressions) convey emotions in classical dance.

q: Which bird has pink beak, grey feathers, and makes a distinct 'Gutar-goo' sound while perching on buildings?
e: Pigeons have grey plumage, pinkish beaks, and make the characteristic gutar-goo call.

q: Why can an owl rotate its head almost 270 degrees around?
a: Its eyes are fixed in socket tubes and cannot turn sideways
w: It lacks a spinal cord near its neck area
Its eyelids remain permanently open during nighttime
Its ears are positioned on its feet instead of its head
e: Owls have fixed eye sockets, requiring them to rotate their entire head to see sideways.

q: In the chapter 'It's Raining', how did Appu the elephant help the wilting banana trees during dry days?
a: He carried water in his trunk and poured it on the roots
w: He dug a deep underground canal from the river to the orchard
He shook rain clouds down directly onto the banana leaves
He splashed muddy river water using his large ears
e: Appu sucked up river water into his trunk and showered it over the banana trees.

q: Which method of cooking involves exposing food directly to dry heat without using oil or water?
e: Roasting cooks food using direct dry heat without water or submerging in fat.

q: Which animal is traditionally used to carry heavy loads and transport people up steep, rocky paths in mountain regions?
e: Mules are sure-footed animals suited for transport across steep mountainous terrain.

q: Which community worker's primary role is maintaining public safety, law, and order in a local area?
e: Police officers are responsible for enforcing law and order in the community.

q: Why do herbivorous animals like cows and buffaloes chew continuously long after they finish grazing?
a: They bring swallowed food back up into their mouth to chew it thoroughly
w: They produce extra milk through continuous jaw movements
They clean their teeth using natural saliva during rest hours
They absorb water directly from the surrounding air by chewing
e: Cows practice rumination, regurgitating cud from their stomach to chew it again.

q: What is Braille script composed of to help visually impaired individuals read by touch?
a: Raised dots arranged in specific grid patterns
w: Carved wooden grooves filled with dark paint
Deeply cut lines stamped into thick paper
Smooth plastic strips with magnetic codes
e: Braille relies on raised dots printed on paper that readers feel with their fingertips.

q: What is the primary pedagogical goal of discussing different family structures in Grade 3 EVS?
a: To build empathy and respect for diverse family setups among children
w: To show that nuclear families are better than joint families
To train students in drawing formal legal family trees for tests
To teach children how to categorize households by income level
e: The topic aims to sensitize children to diverse family structures and avoid stereotypes.

q: What is a 'Taanka' as featured in the chapter 'Drop by Drop'?
a: An underground covered tank built to collect harvested rainwater
w: A deep stepwell used by whole villages to draw groundwater
A raised earthen embankment built across a flowing river
A wooden barrel placed under trees to gather morning dew
e: A Taanka is a traditional underground rainwater harvesting tank used in dry areas like Rajasthan.

q: Why are wet clay pots baked in a kiln or open fire after shaping?
a: To harden the clay and make the pot strong and water-resistant
w: To turn the gray clay into a bright black decorative color
To kill all bacterial germs present inside the natural clay
To make the final pot light enough to float on water
e: Firing changes the chemical structure of clay, rendering it hard, durable, and resistant to water.

q: In which traditional Indian game must a player cross into the opponent's court while holding their breath and continuously chanting a specific word?
e: In Kabaddi, raiders must continuously chant 'Kabaddi' without taking a fresh breath while in the opponent's half.

q: Green leaves prepare food for the plant using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. What gas do plants release into the air during this process?
e: Plants produce oxygen as a byproduct during photosynthesis.

q: In Kashmir, fish is traditionally cooked in which type of oil as described in the Grade 3 EVS chapter 'Foods We Eat'?
e: In Kashmir, mustard oil is commonly used to prepare fish, whereas coconut oil is used in coastal Goa.

q: Why are houses in Assam traditionally built on heavy bamboo or wooden stilts 10 to 12 feet above the ground?
a: To protect homes from flooding during heavy rainfall
w: To prevent hot desert sand from blowing inside
To stop snow from piling up against entrance doors
To keep the house cool during severe summer heatwaves
e: Elevated stilt houses prevent floodwaters during heavy monsoon rains from entering the living areas.

q: Which bird has bright green feathers, a curved red beak, loves to eat green chillies and guavas, and can imitate human voices?
e: Parrots possess green plumage, a curved red beak, a frugivorous diet, and the ability to mimic speech.

q: Which commonly used kitchen spice is botanically a dried unopened flower bud of a plant?
e: Cloves are dried flower buds, whereas ginger is a stem and radish is a root.

q: Which of the following household practices is an appropriate and safe re-use of water used for washing vegetables?
a: Watering potted plants in the garden
e: Greywater from washing vegetables is non-toxic and suitable for watering soil in garden plants.

q: What 6-digit number is included at the end of an Indian address to identify the specific geographic delivery post office?
e: Postal Index Number (PIN) facilitates accurate sorting and delivery of mail to specific regions.

q: Which animal moves completely by crawling or slithering on its belly because it has no legs?
e: Snakes lack limbs and rely on muscular contractions and belly scales to slither along surfaces.

q: Which bird feeds on dead animals, soaring high in the sky and playing a major role in keeping the surroundings clean?
e: Vultures are scavengers that consume animal carcasses, acting as natural environmental cleansers.

q: In the chapter 'Games We Play', which traditional Indian indoor game is played on a cross-shaped board using cowrie shells or dice?
e: Chaupar is a traditional board game played across India using cloth boards and cowrie shells.

q: On a standard map, if a person turns towards their right hand side while facing North, which cardinal direction are they facing?
e: When facing North, East is located directly to the right, West to the left, and South behind.

q: What is a 'Shikara' as described in the EVS chapter on houses?
a: A light wooden boat used as a house or taxi on lakes in Kashmir
w: A high mountain igloo made of ice blocks
A mud hut with a thatched roof made of thorny bushes
A portable tent made of thick yak leather
e: Shikaras are iconic wooden boats found on Dal Lake in Srinagar used for transport and housing.

q: In the chapter 'Chhotu's House', which of the following animals is classified as an uninvited guest living in a human home?
e: Lizards, spiders, and rats inhabit homes uninvited, unlike domestic pets or livestock.

q: Idli and Khaman Dhokla are healthier food items primarily because they are prepared using which cooking method?
e: Steaming cooks food with moist heat without requiring added fats or oil.

q: Which of the following plants has a soft, tender green pseudostem instead of a hard, woody trunk?
e: Banana plants are giant herbaceous plants with green pseudostems rather than true wooden trunks.

q: What core conceptual understanding is introduced through the 'Web of Life' activity at the end of Grade 3 EVS?
a: Interdependence of living and non-living things in nature
w: Mechanical parts of an ecosystem diagram
e: The Web of Life demonstrates how plants, animals, humans, water, air, and sun rely on each other.

q: In the chapter 'A Beautiful Cloth', which of the following garments is worn as a single unstitched piece of fabric?
e: Dupattas, lungis, and sarees are traditional Indian garments worn in their unstitched form.

q: Which community worker is responsible for installing and repairing water pipes, taps, and drainage fittings?
e: Plumbers are skilled tradespeople who work with water supply systems and pipe fixtures.

q: How does an infant who cannot talk yet communicate feelings of hunger or physical distress to caregivers?
e: Infants express basic emotions and biological needs non-verbally through crying and body expressions.

q: According to the chapter 'The Story of Food', seeds from which plant are used both as a tempering spice and to extract cooking oil?
e: Mustard seeds serve as a common spice in Indian tempering and are pressed to yield mustard oil.

q: Why do birds like pigeons, sparrows, and crows lack teeth inside their mouths?
a: They swallow food whole or break it using a beak, grinding it internally
w: They shed all teeth permanently upon reaching adulthood
They only absorb liquid food such as floral nectar
Their teeth are located externally on the edge of their wings
e: Birds lack teeth; their beaks break down food and internal organs like the gizzard grind it up.

q: In the EVS chapter 'Foods We Eat', which regional delicacy made from snakes is mentioned as being popular in Hong Kong?
e: Ling-hu-fen is a popular dish made using snakes in Hong Kong as mentioned in NCERT Grade 3 EVS.

q: Which bird makes deep holes in tree trunks to hide and feed on insects concealed inside the bark?
e: The woodpecker uses its hard beak to peck holes into tree trunks and search for hidden insects.

q: Louis Braille, who developed the tactile script for visually impaired people, belonged to which country?
e: Louis Braille was born in France and created the Braille code after losing his sight as a child.

q: What type of shelter built from blocks of ice is traditionally used in extremely cold polar regions?
e: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter made of compressed ice blocks designed to trap warmth inside.

q: In the chapter 'Games We Play', what is the popular traditional name for the game of Hopscotch played using a marker called a thippi?
e: Stappoo is the common traditional Indian name for the game of Hopscotch.

q: Which set of commonly consumed plant parts are botanically classified as modified taproots?
e: Carrots, radishes, and turnips are swollen taproots that store food underground.

q: What traditional multi-storeyed stepwell structure was historically constructed in India to store and conserve rainwater?
e: A Baoli is a traditional Indian stepwell designed for rainwater collection and public water access.

q: Which cooking fuel is considered the cleanest for domestic indoor use as it produces minimal smoke and soot?
e: Liquefied Petroleum Gas burns efficiently without producing thick smoke or harmful soot.

q: Which plant leaf gives off a strong characteristic aroma when rubbed or crushed between fingers?
e: Mint leaves contain volatile aromatic oils that are easily released when crushed.

q: In India, which major historic city is famous for continuing to run electric trams on its public streets?
e: Kolkata operates the oldest operating electric tram network in Asia.

q: What happens to a letter immediately after a postman collects it from a neighborhood postbox?
a: Taken to the post office for stamping
w: Returned to the sender for verification
e: Letters collected from postboxes are brought to the sorting office to be stamped with the place and date.

q: Why do ducks have webbed skin between their toe digits?
a: To push water efficiently while swimming
w: To catch fast insects in the air
To dig deep burrows in mud
e: Webbed feet act like paddles to help aquatic birds push water and swim efficiently.

q: What is the process of criss-crossing two distinct sets of yarns at right angles on a loom to form fabric?
e: Weaving is the technique of interlacing warp and weft threads to construct woven fabric.

q: Which general characteristic is shared by mammals that give birth to live young instead of laying eggs?
a: Presence of visible external ears and body hair
w: Presence of feathers and hard beaks
Absence of limbs and presence of scales
Presence of moist slippery skin without hair
e: Animals with external ears and hair on their body are generally viviparous and give birth to live young.

q: Which community worker specializes in mending, stitching, and repairing damaged footwear?
e: A cobbler is a skilled tradesperson who repairs shoes and leather footwear.

q: Why does water kept open in a shallow dish evaporate faster on a hot sunny day than on a cloudy cold day?
a: Higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation
w: Clouds push water into the ground
e: Heat energy speeds up the movement of liquid water particles into water vapor.

q: In standard Indian family relationship terms, what is one's mother's brother referred to as?
e: Mama is the Hindi term for one's maternal uncle.

q: Sign language uses structured hand shapes, movements, and facial expressions primarily to help which group communicate?
w: Infants who are learning to walk
e: Sign language is a visual language developed primarily for communication by deaf and hard-of-hearing people.

q: What material is traditionally mixed with sticky wet clay by potters to give strength and prevent pots from cracking while drying?
e: Adding sand or organic Temper like husk prevents clay from shrinking unevenly and cracking during drying.

q: On standard geographical map keys, what is the primary purpose of using standardized symbols?
a: To represent real physical features clearly in small spaces
w: To make maps colorful and decorative
To hide secret locations from travelers
e: Symbols allow complex landmarks like rivers, bridges, and rail lines to be concisely represented on flat maps.

q: Which set of physical features is characteristic of animals that give birth to young ones (viviparous) as taught in Grade 4 EVS?
a: Visible ears and hair on skin
w: Visible ears and feathers on skin
Absence of visible ears and hair on skin
Absence of visible ears and scales on skin
e: Animals with visible external ears and hair on their body generally give birth to live young ones.

q: In a herd of Asian elephants, who leads the herd during movement and foraging?
w: A group of young male elephants
e: An elephant herd is matriarchal and is led by the oldest female.

q: Why is the Khejadi tree well-suited for hot desert regions?
a: It needs minimal water and its wood resists insects
w: It requires constant irrigation to yield sweet fruit
Its sap repels all large wild animals
Its roots retain surface moisture to prevent soil erosion
e: Khejadi trees grow with very little water and their wood is not damaged by insects.

q: Which period of the year is considered ideal for honeybees to lay their eggs in North India?
e: Honeybee queens primarily lay their eggs between October and December.

q: While travelling by train from Gujarat to Kerala, which mountain range is crossed containing many tunnels and bridges?
e: The train route from Gujarat to Kerala passes through the Western Ghats.

q: In which Indian state is the Valley of Flowers National Park located?
e: The Valley of Flowers is situated in the hills of Uttarakhand.

q: What is the primary function of administering Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) during severe diarrhoea?
a: To restore lost fluids and salts
e: ORS helps replenish essential water and minerals lost due to dehydration.

q: What structural role do the hanging branch-like roots of a Banyan tree play?
a: They grow into the ground to support heavy branches
w: They store excess water above ground
They absorb moisture directly from atmospheric air
They extract nutrients from neighboring host plants
e: Hanging roots of a banyan tree reach the soil and provide pillar-like support.

q: The traditional handloom weave called Pochampalli is famous in which Indian state?
e: Pochampalli cloth weaving belongs to the Pochampally district in Telangana.

q: Why is underground water scarcer and more expensive than petrol in Abu Dhabi?
a: The region has sandy terrain with negligible rainfall
w: High local taxes are levied on domestic water usage
Underground water sources are highly polluted by oil
Most fresh water is exported to neighboring nations
e: Abu Dhabi is in a desert region with very little rain and no natural rivers.

q: Which spice, featured in Grade 4 EVS, resembles a small nail and is traditionally used to soothe toothaches?
e: Clove looks like a nail and has medicinal properties for toothache relief.

q: In which bird species does the male build several woven grass nests for the female to choose one?
e: Male weaver birds weave intricate nests, and the female selects the best one to lay eggs.

q: What is the primary objective of serving Mid-Day Meals in primary schools in India?
a: To ensure basic nutrition and improve school attendance
w: To provide health insurance to school children
To offer vocational culinary training to young students
e: Mid-Day Meals promote child nutrition and encourage regular attendance in schools.

q: What common accommodation problem is highlighted in high-density urban slums in Grade 4 EVS?
a: Sharing single public taps and toilets among many families
w: Complete lack of electrical connections in homes
Excessive private garden space in residential units
Total absence of public transport access
e: Slum settlements often share limited common public water taps and sanitation facilities.

q: In which state of India do children commonly use a 'Vallam' (small wooden boat) to reach school?
e: A Vallam is a small wooden boat used in parts of Kerala to cross water bodies.

q: What causes a river's water color to change and become unfit for aquatic life as it flows through towns?
a: Discharge of sewage and industrial effluents
e: Untreated sewage and factory waste alter water quality and harm river ecology.

q: When a child's family relocates to a new city due to a parent's job transfer, what major adjustment is required?
a: Adapting to a new school environment and community
w: Changing the child's hereditary physical traits
Altering the legal citizenship status of the family
Revising the child's extended family relations
e: Relocation forces a child to adapt to new peer groups, schools, and living conditions.

q: In traditional onion farming, what is the specific use of the tool called 'Illige'?
a: Cutting off dry leaves from harvested onions
w: Loosening the soil before sowing seeds
e: An Illige is a sickle-like tool used for cutting dry leaves from harvested onions.

q: What main barrier was removed to help Chuskit, a wheelchair user, reach her school in Ladakh?
a: Leveling the uneven path and building a small ramp
w: Constructing a high suspension cable bridge
e: Smoothing the rough path and creating a ramp enabled her wheelchair to move to school.

q: Where does the Desert Oak tree, found in Australia, store water to survive dry spells?
e: The Desert Oak stores water inside its trunk, which local people can tap using thin pipes.

q: Weightlifter Karnam Malleswari, featured in the Grade 4 EVS curriculum, represents which Indian state?
e: Karnam Malleswari is an Olympic weightlifter who hails from Andhra Pradesh.

q: Which bird uses its chisel-like beak to poke holes in tree trunks to find and extract insects?
e: Woodpeckers have strong chisel-like beaks specifically adapted for pecking into tree bark to feed on hidden insects.

q: In Assam, children often cross rivers using bamboo bridges. What structural property of bamboo makes it suitable for this temporary construction?
a: High tensile strength combined with light weight
e: Bamboo is flexible, light, and possesses high tensile strength, making it ideal for quick bridge construction.

q: The Changpa tribe living in high-altitude regions of Ladakh build cone-shaped tents called 'Rebo'. What material is traditionally woven to make these tents?
e: The Changpa weave strips of yak hair together to stitch strong, warm tent covers known as Rebo.

q: Traditional stepwells called 'Baolis' were primarily constructed across India for what purpose?
e: Baolis were built as communal rain and groundwater storage systems accessible via steps.

q: Sloths sleep for nearly 17 hours a day hanging upside down. Approximately how often do they descend from trees to relieve themselves?
e: Due to extremely slow metabolism, sloths come down from their trees only about once a week.

q: The insectivorous pitcher plant (Nepenthes) traps insects to meet its nitrogen needs. In India, where is it naturally found?
e: Nepenthes is native to the wet, nitrogen-deficient soils of the northeastern state of Meghalaya.

q: In a honeybee colony, what is the primary biological function of the male bees (drones)?
e: Male drones do not gather food or defend the hive; their main role is to mate with the queen.

q: In dry, hot regions like rural Rajasthan, why are mud walls traditionally coated with a mixture of cow dung and mud?
a: To prevent insects from damaging the walls
e: Coating mud walls with cow dung keeps insects away and prevents the dried mud from crumbling.

q: The unique rural transport vehicle called 'Jugad', popular in Gujarat, is traditionally constructed by assembling which components?
a: Front of a motorbike and a rear wooden cart
w: Tractor engine attached to a bamboo cart
Bicycle frame with a small diesel engine
Autorickshaw front with a wooden horse cart
e: A Jugad is made by attaching the front section of a motorcycle to a wooden plank cart at the back.

q: Dr. Beaumont conducted famous experiments on stomach digestion using his patient Martin. What key finding did he discover?
a: Food digests faster inside the stomach than in outside test tubes
w: Digestion completely stops whenever a person feels sad
Food digests at the exact same speed inside and outside
Digestion occurs without needing any stomach digestive juices
e: Dr. Beaumont observed that stomach motion and digestive juices digest food faster inside the stomach than outside in glass tubes.

q: Families working as 'Agariyas' in the Rann of Kutch produce salt during winter primarily from which source?
a: Underground saline water pumped into shallow beds
w: Fresh river water mixed with rock minerals
Mountain rock salt mines dug during winter
Direct rain runoff collected in open storage tanks
e: Agariyas pump underground brackish groundwater into shallow pans where solar evaporation yields salt crystals.

q: In Grade 4 EVS, 'Garam Masala' is introduced as a blend of aromatic ground spices. Which spice is typically NOT part of traditional Garam Masala?
e: Garam Masala consists of warm aromatic spices like cardamom, clove, and cinnamon, while turmeric is added separately to curries.

q: In the NCERT chapter on family dynamics, what is the primary reason behind the shift in Tsering's family structure?
a: His father received a job promotion and transfer
w: His mother started a new home business
His cousin got married and moved in
His family bought a new ancestral house
e: Tsering's family shifts to a new city because his father gets a promotion letter accompanied by a job transfer.

q: Snakes lack external ears and visible ear openings. How do they primarily detect approaching movement on the ground?
a: By feeling vibrations on the ground
w: By smelling air currents through skin
e: Snakes perceive ground-borne vibrations through their lower jaw and body skin contact.

q: When vegetables like radish, carrot, and turnip are harvested and consumed, which modified plant part is eaten?
e: Radish, carrot, and turnip are swollen taproots that store nutrient reserves for the plant.

q: The historical traveler Al-Biruni visited India from Uzbekistan. What feature of Indian engineering did he praise in his writings?
a: Construction of ponds and water reservoirs using massive stones
w: Building of suspension rope bridges over rivers
e: Al-Biruni recorded great praise for how Indians joined heavy rocks with iron clamps to construct water tanks and stepwells.

q: In the Dal Lake area of Srinagar, what is a 'Donga'?
a: A boat house floating on water where local families live
w: A carved wooden door frame in old palaces
A temporary snow igloo built in extreme winter
A stone cellar used for storing winter grains
e: A Donga is a traditional Kashmiri floating house-boat divided into rooms where families reside.

q: When ants move in a neat line toward a food source, how do the following ants navigate the exact route?
a: By smelling chemical scents left on the ground
w: By making clicking sounds with their legs
By sensing the body heat of the front ant
e: Lead ants deposit chemical scents called pheromones on the ground, which trailing ants smell to stay on path.

q: When organic kitchen waste like vegetable peels is buried in moist soil, it turns into rich manure. What carries out this decomposition?
a: Microorganisms in the soil breaking down organic matter
w: Direct absorption of intense solar heat
Evaporation of moisture by wind currents
e: Soil bacteria and fungi act as decomposers, digesting complex organic waste into nutrient-rich compost.

q: How are the ears of birds structurally adapted, explaining why they are not easily visible externally?
a: They are small holes covered by feathers.
w: They are located entirely inside the skull cavity.
They are hidden beneath thick folds of skin.
They are present only during the breeding season.
e: Birds have tiny ear openings on the sides of their head that remain concealed under feathers.

q: Why do mangrove trees growing in coastal mudflats produce specialized roots that grow vertically upwards out of the soil?
a: To absorb atmospheric oxygen directly from the air.
w: To absorb extra sunlight needed for photosynthesis.
To harvest rainwater before it mixes with saline soil.
To anchor the trunk against high oceanic tides.
e: Mangrove breathing roots grow upwards because waterlogged coastal mud lacks sufficient oxygen for root respiration.

q: Which bird is specifically known for using its sharp beak to stitch together two large green leaves to build its nest?
e: The tailorbird uses its needle-like beak to stitch leaves together with plant fibers or spider silk.

q: The district of Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh is nationally famous in the NCERT Grade 4 EVS curriculum for producing which floral item?
e: Kannauj is traditionally renowned across India as a major hub for manufacturing natural flower perfume called Itr.

q: In the NCERT EVS curriculum, the children's council named 'Bheema Sangh' was formed in Holgundi, Karnataka, to solve which community problem?
a: Restoring dried-up village water tanks and wells.
w: Preventing child labor in roadside eateries.
Planting shade trees along state highways.
Distributing mid-day meals during summer holidays.
e: Bheema Sangh was a unique children's panchayat that successfully cleaned and revived a dried-up hill tank for water storage.

q: Why are Fennel seeds (Saunf) traditionally offered after meals in Indian households as noted in EVS lessons?
a: They aid digestion and refresh the breath.
w: They help absorb dietary proteins quickly.
They rapidly elevate blood sugar levels.
e: Fennel seeds contain natural oils that relieve digestive gas and leave a refreshing flavor in the mouth.

q: In heavy rainfall regions like rural Assam, why are houses elevated 10 to 12 feet off the ground on thick wooden pillars?
a: To prevent floodwaters and wild animals from entering.
w: To catch strong upper-altitude winds for cooling.
To keep the house foundation safe from termites.
To create space for parking agricultural carts.
e: Elevated stilt houses protect residents from seasonal floods and ground-dwelling creatures.

q: What is a 'Ferry', as featured in the story of Omana's travel across Kerala?
a: A large boat used to transport people and goods across water.
w: A light wooden cart drawn by bullocks over sand.
A narrow-gauge train running on mountain slopes.
A cable car suspended over deep gorges.
e: Ferries are widely used in Kerala to carry passengers, vehicles, and goods across backwaters and rivers.

q: Anita Khushwaha, highlighted as a 'Girl Star' in Grade 4 EVS, belongs to Bochaha village in which Indian state, where she promoted beekeeping?
e: Anita Khushwaha comes from Bochaha village in the Muzaffarpur district of Bihar.

q: Why is it significantly harder to uproot lawn grass manually than to pull out garden weeds of similar height?
a: Grass roots spread wide and bind soil particles tightly.
w: Grass stems secrete sticky sap into surrounding earth.
Grass forms a deep taproot anchored in hard rock.
Grass leaves lock together to push against pulling force.
e: Grass possesses an extensive fibrous root system that firmly binds topsoil, making manual removal difficult.

q: What physical change occurs when alum (phitkari) is added to a bucket of muddy pond water?
a: Fine suspended mud particles clump together and settle down.
w: Dissolved chemical toxins are completely neutralized.
Disease-causing germs are killed immediately by acid.
Hard minerals evaporate out of the water body.
e: Alum causes fine floating soil particles to aggregate and settle rapidly at the bottom through loading.

q: What primary sensory function do a tiger's sensitive whiskers serve?
a: Detecting fine air movements to navigate and hunt in dark.
w: Regulating body temperature by radiating extra heat.
Measuring water depth while swimming across rivers.
Releasing scent signals to mark territory boundaries.
e: Tiger whiskers are highly sensitive tactile hairs that detect tiny air vibrations, aiding navigation in total darkness.

q: Ghadsisar is a historic water-harvesting structure consisting of nine interconnected lakes built by King Ghadsi. In which city is it located?
e: Ghadsisar was constructed over 600 years ago by King Ghadsi in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, to collect rainwater.

q: Why do water birds like ducks have thin webs of skin between their toes?
a: To push against water efficiently while swimming.
w: To prevent sinking while walking over soft mud.
To catch and hold slippery fish securely.
To grip wet stones tightly when resting.
e: Webbed feet act like paddles, increasing surface area to propel water birds smoothly while swimming.

q: Why do traditional two-storeyed houses in Leh (Ladakh) have no windows on the ground floor?
a: To retain warmth for livestock and stored supplies in winter.
w: To block heavy sandstorms from blowing inside.
To reduce structural weight on wooden support logs.
To maintain privacy from street passersby.
e: The ground floor in Leh homes is used for keeping animals and winter stores, where windowless thick walls keep out harsh cold.

q: Why do vegetable vendors regularly sprinkle water on leafy greens like spinach and coriander throughout the day?
a: To replace lost moisture and prevent wilting.
w: To wash away pesticide residues continuously.
To speed up natural ripening of the leaves.
To increase the weight of vegetables for sale.
e: Water loss via evaporation makes leaves limp; sprinkling water restores cell turgor and maintains freshness.

q: In the traditional onion farming practices of Karnataka described in NCERT Grade 4 EVS, what is the 'Khunti'?
a: An iron rod used to loosen soil around plants.
w: A curved sickle used to trim dry upper leaves.
A bamboo basket used for storing harvested crop.
A wooden seed drill drawn by farm oxen.
e: A Khunti is an iron rod hammered into the soil to loosen hard earth before pulling out mature onions.

q: Amrita Devi Bishnoi sacrificed her life along with fellow villagers to protect Khejarli trees in which present-day state?
e: Amrita Devi Bishnoi led the famous tree-protection sacrifice in Khejarli village near Jodhpur, Rajasthan.

q: Why does a crow build its nest high up on top branches using tough materials like wire pieces and woody twigs?
a: To keep eggs safe from ground-level predators and intrusion.
w: To maximize direct sunlight exposure for egg incubation.
To signal territory size to rival crows during flight.
To allow easy landings during high-speed winds.
e: Crows construct sturdy nests high in tall trees to shield eggs and chicks from ground predators.

q: Why is discarding plastic bags containing leftover food into street garbage dumps particularly hazardous to stray animals?
a: Animals swallow plastic with food, causing fatal gut blockages.
w: Plastic releases harmful gases that burn animal skin.
Plastic deprives nearby soil of all dissolved oxygen.
Plastic attracts poisonous insects that attack livestock.
e: Stray animals often swallow whole plastic bags while eating garbage, leading to intestinal obstruction and death.

q: Which of the following birds can see four times as far as humans can?
e: Kites, eagles, and vultures have specialized binocular vision that allows them to see objects from four times the distance a human can.

q: According to the NCERT Class 5 EVS syllabus, how many types of poisonous snakes are found naturally in India?
e: Only four poisonous snakes are found in India: Cobra, Common Krait, Russel's Viper (Duboiya), and Saw-scaled Viper (Afai).

q: During a lesson on digestion, a teacher asks which digestive enzyme present in saliva starts breaking down carbohydrates in the human mouth. What is the correct answer?
e: Salivary amylase is the digestive enzyme in saliva that begins breaking down complex starches into simpler sugars.

q: Why are large amounts of sugar and salt added when preparing preserved food items like Mamidi Tandra (Aam Papad) or pickles?
a: To reduce moisture content and inhibit microbial growth
w: To enhance the bright color of the preserved food
To speed up the sun-drying process of the pulp
To neutralize natural acids present in ripe fruits
e: High salt and sugar concentrations lower water activity, preventing the growth of bacteria and fungi through osmosis.

q: The insect-trapping plant Nepenthes (pitcher plant) is natively found in which Indian state?
e: In India, Nepenthes species are natively found in the rain-soaked hilly regions of Meghalaya.

q: What is a Johad, traditionally built in arid regions like Rajasthan?
a: A community-built earthen check dam to harvest rainwater
w: An underground room built beneath houses to store ice
A deep stepwell used exclusively for royal bathing
A wooden canal built along steep mountain slopes
e: A Johad is a traditional small earthen check dam designed to collect rainwater and recharge local groundwater.

q: A fresh egg sinks in tap water but floats when a large amount of salt is dissolved in the water. Why does this happen?
a: Dissolving salt increases the density of the water
w: Salt reduces the weight of the egg shell
Salt releases gas bubbles that lift the egg
Salt softens the inner yolk of the egg
e: Adding salt increases the water's density beyond that of the egg, causing the egg to float.

q: Malaria is caused by which microorganism, and which insect acts as its vector?
a: Plasmodium protozoa transmitted by female Anopheles mosquito
w: Dengue virus transmitted by female Aedes mosquito
Salmonella bacteria transmitted by male Anopheles mosquito
Amoeba parasite transmitted by common houseflies
e: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium protozoan, which spreads to humans through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to conquer the peak of Mount Everest?
e: Bachendri Pal reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1984, becoming the first Indian woman to do so.

q: Why were narrow slits and holes built into the high bastions of Golconda Fort?
a: To enable soldiers to see outside safely without exposing themselves to attack
w: To allow monsoon floodwaters to drain out quickly
To encourage cool wind breezes to circulate inside royal rooms
To serve as pigeon holes for sending wartime secret messages
e: Slits in fort walls allowed defending soldiers to view broad surroundings and shoot arrows safely without being exposed to enemy fire.

q: What is the primary scientific reason why astronauts float inside the International Space Station orbiting Earth?
a: The spacecraft and everything inside it are in continuous free fall
w: Earth's gravitational force becomes completely zero in space
Air pressure inside the spacecraft pushes bodies upward
Special magnetic shields in space cancel gravitational attraction
e: Objects in orbit float because the spacecraft and astronauts are in a perpetual state of free fall around Earth, creating microgravity.

q: Which of the following fuels is NOT obtained through the refining of crude petroleum?
e: Biogas is produced by the anaerobic decomposition of biomass, unlike kerosene, diesel, and LPG which are petroleum derivatives.

q: Why do Changthangi goats reared by the Changpa tribe of Ladakh grow an extremely fine undercoat of wool (Pashmina)?
a: To trap air and keep their body warm in severe sub-zero temperatures
w: To reflect intense high-altitude sunlight away from their skin
To shed extra weight so they can climb steep mountain rocks easily
To prevent moisture loss from body pores in dry desert weather
e: Fine undercoat wool traps still air near the skin, acting as an exceptional natural thermal insulator against severe winter cold.

q: When you blow air from your mouth onto your cold hands in winter, your hands feel warm. Why?
a: Exhaled air originates from the warm core body temperature
w: Oxygen reacts chemically with skin moisture to produce heat
Carbon dioxide gas inherently generates friction heat on skin
Speed of exhaled air increases ambient room temperature
e: Human body core temperature is around 37 degrees Celsius, making exhaled air warmer than cold winter air.

q: According to the Right to Forest Act 2007 in India, who holds the legal claim to forest land and its traditional produce?
a: Forest dwellers who have been living in the forest for at least 25 years
w: Private paper manufacturing companies holding government licences
Any Indian citizen who buys agricultural land in a forest area
Local municipal authorities located closest to the forest area
e: The Right to Forest Act 2007 protects communities living in forests for at least 25 years, granting them land rights and produce access.

q: Xanthium seeds possess sharp hooks on their outer surface. How are these seeds primarily dispersed?
a: By clinging to the fur of passing animals or human clothing
w: By floating across water bodies during the rainy season
By drifting long distances on light wind currents
By exploding violently when their seed pods dry up
e: Hooked seeds like Xanthium use epizoochory, sticking to animal fur or human clothes to travel to new locations.

q: In Gregor Mendel's classic genetics experiments on garden pea plants, which seed color trait was observed to be dominant?
e: In garden pea plants (Pisum sativum), yellow seed color is genetically dominant over green seed color.

q: The Dead Sea is famous because swimmers float on it naturally. Roughly how much salt is dissolved in one liter of water in the Dead Sea?
e: The Dead Sea contains approximately 300 grams of salt per liter of water, making it extremely dense.

q: What is a major long-term ecological hazard of monoculture combined with heavy use of chemical fertilizers?
a: Depletion of natural soil fertility and destruction of soil microbes
w: Uncontrolled growth in the local earthworm population
Excessive increase in natural groundwater level
Permanent loss of sunlight absorption capacity in crops
e: Repetitive single-crop farming combined with excessive synthetic fertilizers destroys natural soil organisms and leads to soil degradation.

q: To help students suffering from anemia improve their hemoglobin levels, which set of food items should an EVS teacher recommend?
a: Jaggery, amla, and green leafy vegetables
w: Butter, cheese, and refined wheat flour
Rice, potatoes, and sugary fruit juices
Milk, white bread, and peeled apples
e: Jaggery, amla, and green leafy vegetables are exceptionally rich in iron, which is essential for synthesizing hemoglobin in red blood cells.

q: When ants move in a single file line on the ground, how do the ants following behind stay on the correct path?
a: They follow a chemical scent left by the lead ants.
w: They rely on visual markers on the trail.
They detect heat signals from the ants ahead.
They listen to tiny sound vibrations from the lead ant.
e: Ants drop special chemical scents called pheromones on the ground, which other ants sense to follow the line.

q: The traditional Kalbeliya folk dance and musical performances are historically associated with which community in India?
e: Kalbeliyas are a traditional community of snake charmers from Rajasthan known for their distinct dance mimicking snake movements.

q: Based on Dr. Beaumont's classic experiments on the human stomach recorded in NCERT Class 5 EVS, what is the approximate temperature inside a healthy human stomach?
e: Dr. Beaumont recorded the internal stomach temperature of Alexis St. Martin to be around 30 degrees Celsius.

q: Which combination of environmental conditions causes fungus to grow most rapidly on an exposed slice of bread?
e: Fungal spores thrive, germinate, and multiply best in warm, humid, and moist environments.

q: Who invented Velcro in 1948 after observing seeds with tiny hooks stuck to his clothes and his dog's fur?
e: Swiss engineer George de Mestral invented Velcro after studying burdock seeds clinging to his clothes and dog.

q: According to the Class 5 EVS curriculum on plant origins, which of these common vegetables came to India from South America?
e: Tomatoes, potatoes, and green chillies were introduced to India from South America by South American traders.

q: Which of the following household substances will completely dissolve in water at room temperature without leaving a visible solid residue?
e: Sugar crystals dissolve completely in water to form a uniform, homogeneous solution.

q: Apart from Malaria, which pair of common diseases is also transmitted to humans through mosquito bites?
e: Dengue and Chikungunya are viral infections transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

q: In mountaineering training courses described in Class 5 EVS, what is a key responsibility of a group leader?
a: Stay at the back to assist members who climb slowly
w: Lead from the front to set a fast pace for everyone
Carry all the luggage for every member in the group
Decide the route independently without local guides
e: A mountaineering group leader is responsible for staying behind to guide and support trailing or struggling climbers.

q: Historical cannons found at Golconda Fort were cast from bronze. Bronze is an alloy primarily composed of which two metals?
e: Bronze is a traditional metal alloy made predominantly of copper melted together with tin.

q: Why does liquid water form floating blobs inside an orbiting space station instead of pouring cleanly into a cup?
w: Absence of air pressure inside the station
Rapid freezing of water in space
High magnetic forces pushing molecules apart
e: In an orbiting spacecraft, objects experience weightlessness (microgravity), preventing liquids from flowing downward.

q: How is crude petroleum naturally created deep under the Earth's crust?
a: Decomposition of ancient marine organisms over millions of years
w: Rapid cooling of volcanic lava in freshwater lakes
Chemical reactions between rainwater and iron ore
Underground burning of dense forest trees without air
e: Petroleum forms from dead marine organisms buried under sediment layer upon layer under extreme pressure and heat over millions of years.

q: What is the traditional tent used by the nomadic Changpa tribe of Ladakh called, which is made of woven yak hair?
e: The Changpa tribe lives in large conical tents called Rebo, woven from strips of yak hair stitched together.

q: If an earthquake strikes while students are inside a classroom and cannot evacuate immediately, what is the safest practice?
a: Drop, cover, and hold under a heavy wooden desk or table
w: Stand directly underneath heavy ceiling fans
Rush towards the elevator to go downstairs
Stand right next to glass window panes to look out
e: Taking cover under a sturdy desk protects individuals from falling debris during structural shaking.

q: In Dr. Zakir Husain's story 'Blow Hot, Blow Cold', why did the woodcutter blow air from his mouth onto a freshly roasted potato?
a: To cool the hot potato down
w: To dry up all moisture inside it
e: Air blown from the mouth can feel cooler than very hot food, helping lower the food's surface temperature.

q: In the state of Jharkhand, what does the word 'Torang' mean in the local Kuduk language?
e: In the Kuduk language spoken by tribes in Jharkhand, 'Torang' translates to forest.

q: Which human physical characteristic is an acquired trait rather than a inherited genetic feature from birth parents?
a: A scar from a knife wound
e: A scar is an acquired trait caused by external physical injury and is not coded in parent DNA.

q: When communities are displaced from their ancestral villages to make way for massive dam construction projects, what is the process of setting up their new settlement termed?
e: Rehabilitation refers to providing alternative housing, land, and livelihood options to displaced populations.

q: Before synthetic chemical pesticides were widely available, how did traditional Indian farmers protect stored food grains from insect pests?
a: By mixing dried Neem leaves with stored grains
w: By coating grains with crude petroleum oil
By boiling the seeds in salt water before storage
By sealing the seeds in wet mud containers
e: Dried neem leaves act as a natural insect repellent when mixed into stored food grains.

q: Why do common wall lizards largely disappear from homes across North India during the cold winter months?
a: They enter a state of deep winter sleep (hibernation)
w: They fly away to warm coastal regions
They shed their skin and die before spring
They change their skin color to match dark walls
e: Lizards are cold-blooded animals that go into hibernation during severe winters to conserve energy.

q: How does a male silkworm locate a female silkworm over a distance of several kilometers?
e: Male silkworms have specialized antennae that can detect specific female scents from kilometers away.

q: In traditional Kalbeliya musical performances, which instrument is NOT made from a dried gourd (Lauki)?
e: Been, Tumba, and Kanjari are crafted from dried gourds, whereas Dhol is a wooden membrane instrument.

q: What is the standard ratio for preparing a basic home-made Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS)?
a: One pinch of salt and one teaspoon of sugar in a glass of boiled water
w: Equal amounts of salt and sugar dissolved in ice water
One tablespoon of salt and one teaspoon of sugar in warm water
Two pinches of sugar and half a glass of lemon juice
e: Basic ORS requires one teaspoon of sugar and a pinch of salt dissolved in boiled and cooled water.

q: The 11th-century traveler Al-Biruni came from modern-day Uzbekistan. What feature of traditional Indian engineering did he praise in his travel notes?
w: Intricate wooden palaces built on hilltops
e: Al-Biruni wrote admiringly of India's stepwells (Baolis) and community water conservation structures.

q: Which of the following organisms can be introduced into ponds as a biological control method to eat mosquito larvae?
e: Gambusia (mosquitofish) feed on mosquito larvae in stagnant water, preventing mosquito breeding naturally.

q: An iron nail sinks in water, but a huge ship made of iron floats. What is the main scientific explanation for this?
a: The ship displaces a volume of water whose weight is greater than the total weight of the ship
w: The ship contains trapped helium gas inside its hull
Iron in ships is treated with a chemical waterproof coating
Water exerts buoyant force only on wide objects, not narrow ones
e: A hollow ship displaces a massive volume of water, generating a buoyant force greater than its weight.

q: In historical Indian forts like Golconda, what traditional mechanism was powered by bullocks to lift water to higher elevations?
a: A wheel fitted with multiple clay pots on a chain
w: High-pressure air bellows attached to copper pipes
e: The Persian wheel (Rehat) mechanism used bullock power to rotate a chain of pots and lift water.

q: In the high-altitude cold desert of Ladakh, what is the stone structure built by the Changpa tribe to keep their animals safe called?
e: Rebo is the Changpa family tent, while Lekha is the stone enclosure for their goats and sheep.

q: In Gujarat, the traditional seasonal vegetable dish 'Undhiyu' is prepared in a specific manner. How is it cooked?
a: In an earthen pot sealed and placed upside down among burning coals
w: By deep frying vegetables in mustard oil in an open wok
By boiling grains in a brass vessel over low flame
By steaming chopped vegetables wrapped in banana leaves
e: Undhiyu means 'upside down' in Gujarati, named after the sealed clay pot cooked upside down in charcoal.

q: Which physical adaptation allows coconut seeds to travel long distances across oceans to reach new land?
a: A fibrous and spongy outer cover that traps air
w: Sticky mucilage that adheres to floating wood
Thin membranous wings that catch sea breezes
Sharp hooks that attach to marine animal fur
e: The light, fibrous, and air-trapping husk of a coconut gives it natural buoyancy in water.

q: In the NCERT Class 5 EVS curriculum, Suryamani set up a center named 'Torang'. What is the primary purpose of this initiative?
a: Preserving Adivasi culture, language, music, and knowledge of herbs
w: Training children in modern industrial factory work
Exporting handwoven wooden furniture to foreign markets
e: Suryamani created Torang to uphold Kuduk heritage, Adivasi music, traditions, and forest rights.

q: Which close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, along with his son Narayan, documented efforts to challenge caste discrimination and promote dignity of sanitation work?
e: Mahadevbhai Desai and his son Narayan lived in Gandhi's ashram and actively worked on dignity of labor.

q: The chapter 'Across the Wall' features the story of young female players from the Nagpada Basketball Association in Mumbai. What primary issue does it address?
a: Overcoming gender bias and social stereotypes in sports
w: Addressing language barriers among inter-state migrants
Improving nutrition guidelines for professional athletes
Resolving commercial conflicts between private sports clubs
e: 'Across the Wall' focuses on girls breaking societal gender barriers and stereotypes through sports.

q: Why is Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) considered a preferable choice over petrol and diesel for urban public transport?
a: It emits less smoke and unburnt hydrocarbons upon combustion
w: It is an infinite resource that never runs out
It produces zero carbon dioxide gas when burned
It is derived directly from plant waste rather than fossil reserves
e: CNG is a cleaner-burning fossil fuel that releases fewer harmful pollutants than petrol or diesel.

q: According to the Class 5 EVS textbook, approximately how many hours per day does a sloth spend sleeping while hanging upside down?
e: Sloths live in trees and spend around 17 hours a day sleeping while hanging upside down.

q: Which of these musical instruments works on the principle of blowing air through a narrow column, rather than striking a membrane or string?
e: Shehnai is a wind instrument (aerophone), whereas Dholak and Tabla are percussion and Sitar is stringed.

q: In Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir, what is the traditional intricate wooden ceiling carving found in houseboats called?
e: Khatamband is a traditional Kashmiri woodcraft ceiling design made of interlocking geometric wooden pieces.

q: Why is a patient suffering from severe vomiting and diarrhea given a glucose drip intravenously in a hospital?
a: It delivers immediate energy directly into the bloodstream without needing digestion
w: It neutralizes excess acid formed inside the stomach
It functions as a strong antibiotic to kill harmful microbes
It raises internal body temperature to fight infection
e: Intravenous glucose bypasses the digestive tract to provide instant energy to weak tissues directly.

q: During an earthquake, what is the point on the Earth's surface located directly above the underground point of origin called?
e: The point on the ground surface vertically above the focus (hypocenter) of an earthquake is the epicenter.

q: Which of the following physical characteristics is an inherited genetic trait passed down from parents to offspring?
w: A scar from a surgical operation
Muscular growth developed through gym exercises
e: Earlobe attachment pattern is an inherited genetic trait, unlike acquired scars or learned skills.
